visible_observation: The layout is currently split into a rigid, symmetrical grid. The main title is centered, while the date/venue information is anchored to the bottom-left and the performer list is anchored to the bottom-right. A thin vertical line bisects the canvas, reinforcing this static, balanced separation.
critique: The composition is too tidy and symmetrical for a poster about 'improvisation' and 'noise.' The visual tension is neutralized by the even distribution of text blocks on either side of the center line. The red waveform, which represents the 'noise,' is visually trapped by the text on the right and does not interact dynamically with the rest of the layout. The viewer's eye bounces between two equal corners rather than flowing through a unified hierarchy.
revision: Break the symmetry by shifting the performer list (Nia Cole, Static Bloom, Armand Vale) to the left side, stacking it directly under the date and venue information. This creates a single, strong column of information on the left, allowing the red waveform to sweep unobstructed across the entire bottom right quadrant, creating a diagonal visual path from the title down to the empty space.
protected_strength: The high-contrast neon typography and the visual metaphor of the smooth blue wave transitioning into the jagged red noise must remain the dominant focal point.
